title: WebSocket Endpoint Handling, Connection Managers, and Broadcast Loops

progressiveExplaining.eli5: An HTTP request is like sending a postcard (one message, one reply, connection closed). A WebSocket is like picking up a telephone and leaving the line open forever: both sides can talk and listen at any second. A Connection Manager is the telephone operator keeping track of everyone in the call room and broadcasting messages to all connected phones.
progressiveExplaining.junior: FastAPI provides native WebSocket support: `@app.websocket('/ws/{client_id}') async def ws_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket, client_id: str): await websocket.accept(); ...`. You read with `await websocket.receive_text()` and send with `await websocket.send_text()`. A `ConnectionManager` class tracks active `WebSocket` instances in a list/set and provides `broadcast(message)` to send data to all connected clients.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, WebSocket endpoints operate outside the standard HTTP request/response lifecycle. When `websocket.accept()` executes, the ASGI connection upgrades from HTTP to WebSocket (`scope['type'] == 'websocket'`). Connection state is maintained in-process. For multi-server horizontal scaling, the in-memory Connection Manager must be paired with an external pub/sub message broker (e.g. Redis Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ) to broadcast messages across different server instances.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: Starlette's `WebSocket` class wraps the ASGI `receive` and `send` channels. `websocket.accept()` sends `{'type': 'websocket.accept'}` to complete the handshake. `receive_text()` awaits `receive()` matching `websocket.receive`. When the client closes the connection, `receive()` raises `WebSocketDisconnect(code)`. Handling `WebSocketDisconnect` inside a `try...finally` block ensures the disconnected socket is removed from the manager's active list.

codeComparison.title: Unmanaged Single WebSocket vs Production ConnectionManager
codeComparison.summary: Raw WebSockets without cleanup cause memory leaks on disconnect; a ConnectionManager handles lifecycle and broadcasts.

legacyOrBad.label: Unmanaged WebSocket (Memory Leak)
legacyOrBad.snippet: while True: await ws.receive_text() // ❌ No disconnect handling, leaks on tab close

fullFile.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()

# ❌ OLD: No disconnect handling, no broadcast mechanism, crashes on client close
@app.websocket('/ws')
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
  await websocket.accept()
  while True:
    data = await websocket.receive_text() # ❌ Throws unhandled WebSocketDisconnect on close!
    await websocket.send_text(f'Echo: {data}')

modernOrGood.label: Production ConnectionManager Pattern
modernOrGood.snippet: class ConnectionManager: ... try: ... except WebSocketDisconnect: manager.disconnect(ws) // ✅ NEW

interviewGotchas.question: Can you use FastAPI dependency injection (`Depends()`) inside a `@app.websocket()` endpoint?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of dependency injection across different ASGI protocol scopes.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Yes. FastAPI's `Depends()` works seamlessly in WebSocket endpoints (e.g. for extracting query parameters, cookies, or validating JWT tokens from query strings: `async def ws(websocket: WebSocket, token: str = Depends(get_token))`). If a dependency raises an `HTTPException`, FastAPI automatically closes the WebSocket with an appropriate close code.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: HTTP Authorization headers cannot be passed in standard browser JavaScript `new WebSocket(url)` connections; pass auth tokens via cookies or URL query parameters instead.

interviewGotchas.question: What happens if you broadcast to a dead connection in `manager.broadcast()`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks robust error handling in real-time server loops.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Attempting to `send_text()` to a client that disconnected without triggering a clean close will raise a `RuntimeError: Unexpected ASGI message 'websocket.send'`. Always wrap `connection.send_text()` in a `try...except` block or clean dead connections during broadcast passes.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: A single failed `send_text()` inside a naive `for connection in self.active_connections:` loop will crash the broadcast loop for all other connected users.
